rationale: Baroc-scír (Berkshire) is a place-name element referring to a geographical district or land covered with trees, making forest.n.02 ("land that is covered with trees and shrubs") the better fit as it denotes a tract of land rather than the collective flora (forest.n.01). The scír ('shire/district') component reinforces that this is a territorial/land-based sense rather than the vegetation itself.
